promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Beliefs and teachings: the nature of God and creation
Beliefs and teachings: Jesus Christ and salvation
Practices: the role and mission of the Church

questions.q: Which term describes the Christian belief that God is all-powerful?
questions.explain: Omnipotent means all-powerful, one of the key attributes Christians ascribe to God.

questions.q: What term is used for the Christian belief that God is all-loving?
questions.explain: Omnibenevolent means all-loving or all-good, describing God's perfect love for creation.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the Christian belief in the Trinity?
options: One God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
God, Jesus and the Virgin Mary
The union of the Old and New Testaments
questions.explain: The Trinity is the belief in one God existing as three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Why does the problem of evil challenge traditional Christian beliefs about God?
options: Suffering seems to conflict with God being both all-powerful and all-loving
It proves God does not know the future
It shows God is only present in heaven
It demonstrates that Jesus was not divine
questions.explain: If God is omnipotent and omnibenevolent, the existence of evil and suffering appears difficult to reconcile.

questions.q: According to the Genesis creation account, over how many days did God create the world before resting?
questions.explain: Genesis describes God creating over six days and resting on the seventh.

questions.q: In John's Gospel, 'In the beginning was the Word' — who do Christians understand the Word (Logos) to be?
questions.explain: The Word (Logos) refers to Jesus, present with God at creation and later made flesh.

questions.q: What is the Christian belief that God became human in the person of Jesus called?
questions.explain: The Incarnation is the belief that God took human form in Jesus Christ.

questions.q: What term describes Jesus rising from the dead on the third day?
questions.explain: The Resurrection is the belief that Jesus rose from the dead, central to Christian faith.

questions.q: What is the term for Jesus returning to heaven after his resurrection appearances?
questions.explain: The Ascension is the belief that Jesus was taken up into heaven forty days after the Resurrection.

questions.q: What do Christians mean by atonement?
options: The reconciliation of God and humanity through Jesus' death
The forgiveness given to Adam and Eve
Jesus' second coming to judge the world
The pouring of water at baptism
questions.explain: Atonement is the restoring of the relationship between God and humanity, achieved through Jesus' sacrifice.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the Christian idea of salvation by grace?
options: Salvation is a free, undeserved gift from God, not earned by good works
Salvation must be earned through good deeds alone
Salvation is available only to church ministers
Salvation is achieved solely by going on pilgrimage
questions.explain: Grace is God's freely given love and forgiveness, which cannot be earned by human effort.

questions.q: A Christian says, 'I am forgiven not through my own efforts but through Jesus' sacrifice on the cross.' Which belief is she expressing?
questions.explain: She expresses that salvation comes as God's gift through Jesus' atoning death, not by human works.

questions.q: Which best describes liturgical worship?
options: Structured worship following a set order or liturgy
Spontaneous worship with no fixed pattern
Worship expressed only through charitable giving
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a formal, set structure, such as the Eucharist in Catholic and Anglican churches.

questions.q: Which sacrament involves sharing bread and wine in memory of Jesus' Last Supper?
questions.explain: The Eucharist (Holy Communion) uses bread and wine to recall Jesus' Last Supper and sacrifice.

questions.q: In baptism, what does the use of water primarily symbolise?
options: Cleansing from sin and new life in Christ
The fire of the Holy Spirit
The bread of the communion meal
questions.explain: Water in baptism symbolises the washing away of sin and the beginning of new life as a Christian.

questions.q: Parents bring their newborn baby to church, where the priest pours water over the child's head. Which practice is this?
questions.explain: Pouring water over a baby's head is infant baptism, practised in Catholic and Anglican churches.

questions.q: In which country is the Christian pilgrimage site of Iona located?
questions.explain: Iona is a small island off the west coast of Scotland and a well-known place of Christian pilgrimage.

questions.q: What key event do Christians celebrate at Easter?
options: The coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost
questions.explain: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, the most important Christian festival.

questions.q: A local church runs a food bank and a night shelter for homeless people. This best demonstrates which aspect of Christian practice?
options: The role of the Church in serving the local community
questions.explain: Providing food banks and shelters shows the Church putting Christian teaching into action to help the local community.

questions.q: A Christian travels to Lourdes in France hoping for spiritual renewal and healing. This is an example of which practice?
questions.explain: Travelling to a holy site such as Lourdes for spiritual purposes is an act of pilgrimage.
